I think You did well
I tried it here and it worked

Goal
* The statement is a little too long for a clash of code. Consider simplifying the background story.

* The Wikipedia link to the Caesar cipher could be removed or at least moved to the end and labelled as "Optional reference".

* Please change "<<HH:MM>>" to "[[HH]]{{:}}[[MM]]".

* Please change "the word FRIEND" to "the substring FRIEND" to avoid suggesting that the task involves identifying individual words in the [[message]].

* Please state that the hour component is ignored.

* Please clarify that the shift wraps around from {{Z}} to {{A}}.

* In the final paragraph, please change 0 to 1.

* Please format 1, 25, 00, 59 and 26 as {{constants}}.

Input
* Please change "<<HH:MM>>" to "[[HH]]{{:}}[[MM]]".

Constraints
* Please add:
00 ≤ [[HH]] ≤ 23
00 ≤ [[MM]] ≤ 59

Stub generator
* Please add a write statement, e.g. write answer.

Cases
* Each test and its corresponding validator should cover the same scenario. Therefore, it seems inconsistent to use different case names for the test and validator in Pairs 1, 2, and 4.

* More generally, the case names appear to serve a decorative purpose, since the hour component is irrelevant to the task.

* The coverage is mostly satisfactory, but please modify or add cases to cover the following minute values and letters not yet represented:

  • Visible tests: 6, 20, 23, 26, 42, 44, 53, 59 (e.g. change one of the 32 minute values to 06); Q, Z.

  • Hidden validators: 55, 56; J, Q, Z.

Thanks.

Wow, well done

I could code a solution in JavaScript and had no problems

I would approve, but I'll wait for @5DN1L :p
Thanks for the thorough feedback!! I'll work on updating these items
Requested changes have been applied. All tests now cover the full ranges A-Z and 00-59, and all validators cover the same ranges.

The updated cases look good now. There are only two remaining points:

Goal
* The statement is a little too long for a clash of code. Consider simplifying the background story.

* Please clarify that the parsed minute values shown in the example are the remainders after applying modulo 26.

Thanks.
